goals.goal: Quais são as regras de ownership em Rust e por que atribuir uma String a outra variável invalida a original?

nuggets.text: Rust ownership rule: each value in Rust has an owner.
Rust ownership rule: there can only be one owner at a time.
Rust ownership rule: when the owner goes out of scope, the value is dropped.
After a `String` is assigned to another variable, Rust considers the original variable no longer valid because the value was moved.
Moving a `String` avoids a double free error, which would happen if both variables tried to free the same memory when going out of scope.
Variables of types that implement the `Copy` trait are trivially copied instead of moved and remain valid after assignment to another variable.

goals.goal: Como funciona o tratamento de erros com Result em Rust: unwrap, expect e o operador ?

nuggets.text: The Result enum is defined as `enum Result<T, E> { Ok(T), Err(E) }`.
`unwrap` returns the value inside `Ok` if the Result is `Ok`.
`unwrap` calls the `panic!` macro if the Result is `Err`.
`expect` lets you choose the `panic!` error message.
The `?` operator placed after a Result returns the value inside `Ok` and the program continues if the Result is `Ok`.
The `?` operator returns the `Err` from the whole function, as if `return` had been used, if the Result is `Err`.
Using `?` in a function that returns `()` does not compile and fails with error E0277.

goals.goal: Como criar, ativar e desativar um ambiente virtual em Python e congelar as dependências num requirements.txt?

nuggets.text: A virtual environment is created with `python -m venv` followed by the path of the new environment directory.
On Unix or macOS a virtual environment is activated with `source <venv>/bin/activate`.
On Windows a virtual environment is activated by running the `Scripts\activate` script inside the environment directory.
An active virtual environment is deactivated by running `deactivate`.
`python -m pip freeze > requirements.txt` writes the installed packages to requirements.txt.
`python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` installs all the packages listed in requirements.txt.
Creating a venv places a `pyvenv.cfg` file in the target directory with a `home` key pointing to the Python installation the command was run from.

goals.goal: Qual a diferença entre var, let e const em JavaScript quanto a escopo, hoisting e reatribuição?

nuggets.text: `var` declares a variable in the entire function scope, or globally outside functions, regardless of block scope.
`let` declares a variable limited to the scope of the block where it is used.
`var` declarations are hoisted: a variable can appear to be used before it is declared.
`const` creates a block-scoped variable whose value cannot be changed by assignment.
Variables declared with `let` are hoisted to the start of the block in which they are defined.
A `const` cannot be redeclared.
A `const` declaration without an initializer throws a SyntaxError.
`const` does not make the value immutable, only the binding: an object's contents can still change.

goals.goal: Como funciona o git rebase e quando não devo usá-lo?

nuggets.text: `git rebase` takes the changes committed on one branch and replays them on a different branch.
To rebase a branch onto another, check out the branch and run `git rebase` with the target branch.
Rebasing abandons existing commits and creates new ones that are similar but different.
Rule: do not rebase commits that exist outside your repository and that people may have based work on.
If others based work on commits that were later rewritten by a rebase and pushed, the collaborators have to re-merge their work.
`git rebase` works by going to the common ancestor of the current branch and the target branch.
`git rebase` gets the diff introduced by each commit of the current branch and applies each change in turn on top of the target.
`git rebase --onto` replays a branch's patches since it diverged from another branch as if it were based directly on a different branch.

goals.goal: Quais obrigações e direitos da LGPD um desenvolvedor precisa considerar: direitos do titular, encarregado, incidentes de segurança e multas?

nuggets.text: LGPD Art. 18: the data subject has the right to obtain confirmation of the existence of processing from the controller.
LGPD Art. 18: the data subject has the right to access the data processed by the controller.
LGPD Art. 18: the data subject has the right to correction of incomplete, inaccurate or outdated data.
LGPD Art. 18: the data subject has the right to portability of the data to another service or product provider.
LGPD Art. 41: the controller must appoint a data protection officer (encarregado).
LGPD Art. 41: the identity and contact information of the encarregado must be publicly disclosed, preferably on the controller's website.
LGPD Art. 48: the controller must notify the national authority (ANPD) of a security incident that may cause relevant risk or damage to data subjects.
LGPD Art. 48: the controller must notify the data subject of a security incident that may cause relevant risk or damage to data subjects.
LGPD Art. 52: a simple fine can be up to 2% of the company's revenue in Brazil in its last fiscal year.
LGPD Art. 52: the simple fine is limited in total to R$ 50,000,000.00 per infraction.

goals.goal: Como escrever uma expressão de agendamento no crontab: quais são os cinco campos, seus intervalos e atalhos como @reboot e @daily?

nuggets.text: The crontab minute field accepts values from 0 to 59.
The crontab hour field accepts values from 0 to 23.
The crontab day of month field accepts values from 1 to 31.
The crontab month field accepts values from 1 to 12, or names.
The crontab day of week field accepts values from 0 to 7, or names.
In the day of week field, both 0 and 7 mean Sunday.
An asterisk (*) in a crontab field always stands for "first-last".
`@reboot` runs the job once after reboot.
`@daily` runs the job once a day, equivalent to `0 0 * * *`.
When both the day of month and day of week fields are restricted, the command runs when either field matches the current time.

goals.goal: O que é o Pix, quem o oferece, quando foi lançado e onde está a especificação da API Pix?

nuggets.text: Pix is an instant money transfer and instant electronic payment method in Brazilian reais (R$).
Pix is offered by the Banco Central do Brasil (central bank).
Pix is offered to individuals and companies.
Pix operates 24 hours a day without interruption.
Pix's initial release date was 5 October 2020.
Pix was officially launched in full on 16 November 2020.
The Pix API functional specification is published in the bacen/pix-api GitHub repository.
The Pix API specification in the bacen/pix-api repository uses the OpenAPI 3.0 format.
